input.title: Restore the workflow scheduler after a database outage
body: Use this guide when the scheduler has stopped because its database was unavailable and the database is now back. It brings the scheduler back without losing queued jobs.
## Prerequisites
- Access to the machine that runs the scheduler.
- A running database that accepts connections.
## Steps
1. Check that the database accepts connections: `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select 1"`.
2. Start the scheduler: `docker compose up -d scheduler`.
3. Open the scheduler log and wait for the line that says lease recovery has finished.
## Expected result
The scheduler reports that it is ready, and jobs that were queued before the outage start running again.
## Troubleshooting
- If step 1 fails, the database is still unreachable. Fix that first and repeat the guide.
- If jobs do not resume, look in the log for lease errors and ask the operator on call.

input.title: Train and evaluate the reinforcement learning agent
body: Use this guide to train the agent on the sample environment and to measure how well it plays. A run takes about 20 minutes on one GPU.
## Prerequisites
- Python 3.11 and the packages in `requirements.txt`.
- One GPU with at least 8 GB of memory.
## Steps
1. Pick a seed. The examples use 7.
2. Train: `python train.py --seed 7 --steps 200000`.
3. Evaluate on the held-out episodes: `python evaluate.py --seed 7 --episodes 100`.
## Expected result

Training writes a model file to `runs/seed-7/`. The evaluation prints the mean score and the spread over the 100 episodes. Scores differ a little between seeds, so report at least three seeds before comparing agents.
## Troubleshooting
- If training stops with an out-of-memory error, lower the batch size in `config.yaml`.
- If two runs with the same seed differ, check that no other process shares the GPU.
